newsitem.title: RUSSIA: RUSSIA BOND PRICES EASE, INDIVIDUALS BUY DOLLARS.
newsitem.headline: RUSSIA BOND PRICES EASE, INDIVIDUALS BUY DOLLARS.

text.p: Russian OFZ discount government bond prices fell on Thursday afternoon, reversing an upward morning trend on central bank intervention, dealers said.
The rouble edged down as individuals rushed to buy dollars on fears over the announced redenomination of the rouble, they said.
*Average yield on taxed OFZ bonds fell to 27.13 pct from 27.79 pct on Tuesday
*Average yield on taxed T-bills was unchanged at 18.30 pct
*Turnover rose to 3.570 trln rbls from 2.966 trln rbls
*Central bank sold 156 bln rbls of bills, bonds
*Banks transferred 2.83 trln rbls for trading

"One could feel demand for all issues in the morning," Rossiisky Kredit dealer Konstantin Svyatny said. "But later, the central bank started selling to slow down the growth and sellers followed. A choppy selling began."
He said Baltic banks may have encouraged the selling trend as they tried to raise cash by selling Russian paper.
St Petersburg tax police have recently suspended correspondent accounts of Baltic states banks, saying they had seriously violated banking and hard currency laws.
One forex trader said households were buying $50-$70 million with roubles daily after Russia said on Monday the rouble would be redenominated from January 1, 1998.
Another dealer who said individual dollar buying had picked up also said dollar appreciation was seasonal.
"The trend for the growth of the dollar is seasonal. The second half of the year starts (and) new hard currency contracts are signed," the dealer said.
--Anna Smirnova, Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520
